transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you lately or what brings you in today?

I guess what brings me in is… I just can’t shake this feeling I’ve been carrying around. It’s like this heavy mix of fear and guilt that’s there most of the day. I’m tense all the time, like I’m waiting for something else to go wrong, even when nothing is actually happening right then.

And I keep going over it in my head, blaming myself for not stopping what happened. I know sitting here saying that maybe sounds simple, but it doesn’t feel simple. It’s like my body and my brain won’t let it go, and I’m just tired of feeling on edge and responsible all the time.
Have you ever felt down or lost interest in things you used to enjoy during this time?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean… I have felt worn down, definitely, but I don’t know if I’d call it “down” in the way you mean. It’s more like I’m drained from being tense so much, if that makes sense.

As far as losing interest in things, I haven’t really noticed it as the main thing. Like, I still know what I like, I just sometimes don’t feel as relaxed doing things because my mind is elsewhere. But I wouldn’t say I’ve completely stopped caring about everything or anything like that. It’s more that everything feels harder to settle into.
Do you find yourself worrying about a number of different things — like work, relationships, or other responsibilities — and does that worry feel hard to control?

I don’t know that it’s a bunch of different things, exactly. I mean, I do worry about normal stuff like anyone does, like work or keeping up with responsibilities, but that’s not really what feels out of control to me.

It’s more… my mind gets stuck on certain things, and then everything else kind of gets filtered through that. So if I’m distracted at work or short with someone, I might start thinking, “What’s wrong with me?” or “Why can’t I just handle this better?” But I wouldn’t say I’m lying awake making lists of every possible problem in my life or worrying equally about money, relationships, work, all of that.

So I guess my answer is… not really, at least not in the general way you’re asking. It’s not like I’m constantly worrying about every category of life. It’s more specific than that, and it feels harder to shut off when it starts.
Have you been having intrusive thoughts, memories, or moments where you feel like you’re re-living a specific event that was upsetting or traumatic for you?

Yeah… yes. That does happen. It’s not constant, but when it happens it feels so sudden that it kind of knocks the air out of me.

Like, because of my work, I’ll be doing something completely ordinary — measuring a railing, checking a stair opening, looking at a landing — and then there’ll be this sound, like a ladder scraping against concrete or metal, and it’s like my brain just… jumps. Out of nowhere I can see my husband falling, like it’s happening right in front of me again. Not like I’m choosing to think about it or remembering it in a normal way. It’s more like it interrupts whatever I’m doing.

My stomach drops immediately, and my hands get shaky, which is embarrassing when I’m trying to hold a tape measure or write something down. I’ll try to tell myself, “You’re here, you’re just at work, this is a different site,” but for those few moments it feels very real, like my body hasn’t caught up to the fact that it’s not happening right then.
Do these intrusive thoughts or flashbacks only happen in relation to that specific event with your husband, or do they sometimes involve other situations or events too?

It’s really tied to that specific thing with my husband. I mean, I can get startled or uneasy in other situations, but when I’m talking about those really vivid moments — the ones where it feels like it’s happening right in front of me — it’s him falling.

It’ll be something so ordinary at work, like I’m measuring a railing or standing near a stair opening, and then I hear a ladder scrape or some metal sound, and suddenly my mind just goes straight there. I can see it, like not just “remembering,” but almost like it’s in front of me for a second. My stomach drops, my hands get shaky, and I have to kind of force myself to look around and remind myself where I actually am.

I don’t really have that same kind of flashback about other events, not in that way. It’s mostly that one.
